questions.q: When others plotted against the Prophet and his Companions, what course did the Quran set for them?
options: Withdraw from all contact with others
Not quite. The article says: Trust in God, rise above the situation and carry on with positive work.
Wait until the opponents grew tired
Not quite. The article says: Trust in God, rise above the situation and carry on with positive work.
Trust in God, rise above the situation and carry on with positive work
Yes. No room was left for negative thinking.
Uncover each plot and answer it in kind
Not quite. The article says: Trust in God, rise above the situation and carry on with positive work.
questions.rationale: “Ignoring the plots and antagonism, trusting only in God and rising above circumstances, they were to continue all activities which were of a positive nature.”

questions.q: What does the article say happens to someone obsessed with the idea that everyone is against him?
options: He loses objectivity – like a man who sees only the thorns in a garden of roses
Well read. He even suspects his own well-wishers.
He learns to trust more easily
Not quite. The article says: He loses objectivity – like a man who sees only the thorns in a garden of roses.
He gains many new allies
Not quite. The article says: He loses objectivity – like a man who sees only the thorns in a garden of roses.
He becomes more alert and successful
Not quite. The article says: He loses objectivity – like a man who sees only the thorns in a garden of roses.
questions.rationale: “One loses all objectivity in thinking… One becomes like the man who can see only the thorns in a garden of roses.”

questions.article: Growing Old Is Certainly Not a Countdown
questions.q: The article says ageing is “not the beginning of a countdown.” What is it, then?
options: A “count-up” – a time of maturity and wisdom that can guide the next generation
Right. “Old is gold.”
A burden to be endured
Not quite. The article says: A “count-up” – a time of maturity and wisdom that can guide the next generation.
A time to withdraw completely
Not quite. The article says: A “count-up” – a time of maturity and wisdom that can guide the next generation.
A time only for rest
Not quite. The article says: A “count-up” – a time of maturity and wisdom that can guide the next generation.
questions.rationale: “Ageing is not the beginning of a countdown, but is rather, the time for a count-up. The world can benefit greatly from the planning skills and wisdom of the aged.”

questions.article: Growing Old Is Certainly Not a Countdown
questions.q: What does the article call the key aspect of old age?
options: Freedom from learning
Not quite. The article says: Maturity, not longevity.
Maturity, not longevity
Yes. Experience ripens thinking.
Physical strength
Not quite. The article says: Maturity, not longevity.
Leisure
Not quite. The article says: Maturity, not longevity.
questions.rationale: “The key aspect of old age is maturity, not longevity.”

questions.q: Bertrand Russell traced man’s philosophical quest to the “terror of cosmic loneliness.” How does the article explain that loneliness?
options: The need for God is woven into human nature, and only finding Him fills the inner vacuum
Well reasoned. A rock feels no such lack.
It comes from living in large cities
Not quite. The article says: The need for God is woven into human nature, and only finding Him fills the inner vacuum.
It is caused by too much study
Not quite. The article says: The need for God is woven into human nature, and only finding Him fills the inner vacuum.
It disappears with age
Not quite. The article says: The need for God is woven into human nature, and only finding Him fills the inner vacuum.
questions.rationale: “A human being by his very nature has interwoven in him the desire to submit to God… His feeling of loneliness or the sense of vacuum in his life is fulfilled by his discovery of and belief in God.”

questions.q: A large sum reached Madinah and Umar wished to distribute it fairly. Whose suggestion did he adopt?
options: His own first plan, unchanged
Not quite. The article says: Walid ibn Hisham’s – to compile registers, as he had seen done in Syria.
A plan to give it only to the elders
Not quite. The article says: Walid ibn Hisham’s – to compile registers, as he had seen done in Syria.
A proposal to store it for war
Not quite. The article says: Walid ibn Hisham’s – to compile registers, as he had seen done in Syria.
Walid ibn Hisham’s – to compile registers, as he had seen done in Syria
Correct. A good method was welcome from any quarter.
questions.rationale: “‘I saw that the rulers there had compiled registers for this purpose…’ Umar accepted this advice and delegated the task of compiling registers to three of his Companions.”

questions.q: Before giraffes were flown from Kenya, they were played recordings of jet engines for weeks. What does the article compare with this preparation?
options: Schooling before a career
Not quite. The article says: The guidance of prophets and scriptures, which accustoms man to the conditions of the next world before he arrives.
Training before a race
Not quite. The article says: The guidance of prophets and scriptures, which accustoms man to the conditions of the next world before he arrives.
The guidance of prophets and scriptures, which accustoms man to the conditions of the next world before he arrives
Yes. To spare him the shock of arriving unprepared.
Packing before a holiday
Not quite. The article says: The guidance of prophets and scriptures, which accustoms man to the conditions of the next world before he arrives.
questions.rationale: “God sends His prophets to teach man the conditions that will prevail in the eternal world for which he is bound… and adopt its conditions before he gets there.”

questions.q: In what way, says the article, will the next world differ from this one?
options: It will be much like this one, only longer
Not quite. The article says: Only the real worth of one’s deeds will count; clever words and unfair means will carry no weight.
Excuses will be accepted more readily
Not quite. The article says: Only the real worth of one’s deeds will count; clever words and unfair means will carry no weight.
Only the real worth of one’s deeds will count; clever words and unfair means will carry no weight
Right. Perfect justice will prevail.
Success there will depend on rank
Not quite. The article says: Only the real worth of one’s deeds will count; clever words and unfair means will carry no weight.
questions.rationale: “In the next world there will be only one basis of success, and that will be the real worth of one’s own actions.”

questions.q: A good tree has firm roots and branches in the sky. What principle of change does the article take from it?
options: First consolidation, then expansion – begin with the individual before changing society
Exactly. Otherwise one builds sandcastles.
Spread widely before taking root
Not quite. The article says: First consolidation, then expansion – begin with the individual before changing society.
Change institutions first, people later
Not quite. The article says: First consolidation, then expansion – begin with the individual before changing society.
Grow upward as fast as possible
Not quite. The article says: First consolidation, then expansion – begin with the individual before changing society.
questions.rationale: “Real change in human life can be brought about by following a principle demonstrated in the natural world: first consolidation and then expansion.”

questions.q: People differ in ability and success, and envy follows. What attitude does the article ask for?
options: Insist that everyone achieve the same
Not quite. The article says: Put away envy and spite, give honour where it is due, and see all as equal before God.
Hide one’s own success
Not quite. The article says: Put away envy and spite, give honour where it is due, and see all as equal before God.
Put away envy and spite, give honour where it is due, and see all as equal before God
Well read. “All men descend from Adam.”
Avoid those who do better
Not quite. The article says: Put away envy and spite, give honour where it is due, and see all as equal before God.
questions.rationale: “We must discard hardened attitudes of envy, bitterness, spite, and… look upon ourselves and our fellow-men as being equal in the eyes of God.”
